rows.citation: Duston T, Xin S, Sun Y, et al. (2025). AInsteinBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents on Scientific Repositories. arXiv preprint arXiv:2512.21373.
rows.model_type: general scientific software repositories (PySCF, Qiskit, RDKit, OpenMM, AMReX, Einstein Toolkit); no neuroscience codebases
rows.controlled_mutations: no; tasks come from real maintainer pull requests with fail-to-pass tests, not systematically generated single-fault mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no; correctness is judged by repository unit tests, not by stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no; no neuron models or electrophysiological features are involved.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; no selection or minimisation of test or protocol sets is described.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; a benchmark for scoring agents, with no discovery/held-out split for choosing tests.
rows.ai_transformations: yes; LLM agents edit real scientific repositories in Docker and are scored by tests; authors note tests can be imperfect scientific oracles.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Measures agent coding ability on non-neuroscience repositories via unit tests. NeuroSem asks whether edited neuron models keep their behaviour across stimulation protocols; agents are only a secondary case study there.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abstract page citation meta tags and submission history (v1 2025-12-24); arXiv HTML full text (repository list, test-based evaluation, GitHub link); GitHub REST API via gh for repository and licence. arXiv export API returned a rate-limit error.
rows.found_via: WebSearch LLM coding agents neuroscience query; arXiv abstract page metadata

rows.citation: Li M, Yang X, Liu J, et al. (2026). Domain-Validity-Gated Metamorphic Testing of Scientific ML Surrogates. arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.17529.
rows.model_type: scientific ML surrogates (MeshGraphNets cylinder-flow and airfoil CFD, FNO Burgers/heat PDE surrogates); not neuroscience
rows.controlled_mutations: partial; an author-implemented 10-mutant seeded-fault catalogue is a secondary stress test of the metamorphic-relation detectors.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; several metamorphic relations (node permutation, mirror symmetry, divergence) act as distinct probes; not electrical stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no; metrics are flow-field and conservation residuals, not electrophysiology.
rows.protocol_optimization: unclear; a minimum MR subset audit artifact is mentioned, but no greedy or cost-matched selection was found in the scanned text.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial; verdicts replicated on held-out trajectories, a checkpoint roster and further architectures; no held-out fault family for a selected test set.
rows.ai_transformations: partial; LLM and LLM-simulated-expert candidate relations serve as secondary baselines; no AI edits of models are evaluated.
rows.software: replication package https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20702952 (DOI resolves at doi.org; Zenodo record API timed out, so contents and licence are unverified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest on tolerance gating: a relation is admitted only when its tolerance exceeds the operator's O(h) numerical floor. NeuroSem would apply refinement-derived floors to neuron electrophysiology features, adding mutant-calibrated protocol selection and held-out models and families.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abstract page citation meta tags and submission history (v1 2026-06-16); arXiv HTML full text (seeded-fault catalogue, operator-floor sweep, baselines, data availability); doi.org resolution of the Zenodo DOI (302 to Zenodo; record page 504).
rows.found_via: WebSearch metamorphic testing scientific simulation query; arXiv abstract page metadata

rows.citation: Korngreen A (2025). Sensitivity analysis of voltage-gated ion channel models. bioRxiv.
rows.model_type: Markov gating models of voltage-gated ion channels (open probability under voltage protocols); channel level, not whole neurons
rows.controlled_mutations: no; kinetic parameters are sampled over ranges for Sobol analysis rather than introduced as discrete recorded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; compares voltage steps with multi-frequency sinusoids (20-200 Hz); v2 finds sinusoids keep the step-protocol sensitivity ranking.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no; output is channel open probability, not current-clamp spike or subthreshold features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no; gives qualitative advice on informative protocols but no algorithmic protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no; no discovery/held-out split; convergence checked by repeating analyses at N=512 and N=2048.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-assisted edits are involved.
rows.software: MarkovSensitivity https://github.com/alon67/MarkovSensitivity (MIT per GitHub API); built on SALib
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Background on how model structure limits which parameter changes are visible at channel level. NeuroSem tests whole-neuron edits empirically across current-clamp protocols. The v2 findings temper the input note: sinusoidal stimulation did not change which parameters mattered.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (title, author, bioRxiv, 2025); bioRxiv details API (v1 2025-08-06, v2 2026-02-27, CC BY-NC-ND); Europe PMC abstract; bioRxiv v2 JATS XML via API (the bioRxiv site returned error 1015); GitHub REST API via gh.
rows.found_via: WebSearch global sensitivity analysis query; Europe PMC refined sensitivity query; Crossref

rows.citation: Meliza CD, Kostuk M, Huang H, et al. (2014). Estimating parameters and predicting membrane voltages with conductance-based neuron models. Biological Cybernetics, 108(4), 495-516.
rows.model_type: single-compartment Hodgkin-Huxley conductance model of zebra finch HVC neurons fitted to slice recordings
rows.controlled_mutations: no; variational data assimilation estimates parameters; no seeded model faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; fits on one 1,500 ms complex current waveform, then compares predictions under novel injected currents.
rows.electrophysiology_features: unclear; the abstract reports voltage prediction only; full text is closed access and was not read.
rows.protocol_optimization: unclear; the abstract mentions a complex waveform; the input's claimed stimulus-design criteria were not verifiable from accessible text.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial; models are tested on novel injected currents (held-out stimuli), not held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-assisted edits are involved.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Builds and validates models against recordings using held-out currents. NeuroSem compares a reference model with its edited version, using calibrated tolerances and a selected protocol battery to find behavioural drift.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (authors, venue, volume/issue/pages, 2014); Europe PMC core record with PMID 24962080 and abstract; OpenAlex (closed access, no repository full text); Springer landing page (abstract only).
rows.found_via: WebSearch data assimilation Abarbanel query; PubMed esummary

rows.citation: Nogaret A, Meliza CD, Margoliash D, et al. (2016). Automatic Construction of Predictive Neuron Models through Large Scale Assimilation of Electrophysiological Data. Scientific Reports, 6, 32749.
rows.model_type: nine-ion-channel single-compartment conductance model of zebra finch HVC neurons fitted to recordings
rows.controlled_mutations: no; parameters are estimated by IPOPT constrained optimisation; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes; 20-50 current protocols per neuron, mixing Lorenz-chaotic waveforms with steps, plus step-only protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no; objective is least-squares voltage misfit and validation predicts voltage traces; no feature extraction found in the scanned text.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial; waveforms are designed with the bandwidth to constrain time constants, but no subset of protocols is algorithmically selected.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial; completed models predict responses to protocols outside the assimilation window; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-assisted edits are involved.
rows.software: none released identified; uses IPOPT with Sympy-derived derivatives
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Designs broadband currents to fit parameters from data and checks prediction on other protocols. NeuroSem selects a small protocol battery that exposes differences between a reference model and single-fault edits.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (authors, venue, volume, article number, abstract); nature.com open-access full text (protocol design, IPOPT methods).
rows.found_via: WebSearch data assimilation Abarbanel query; Crossref

rows.citation: Oesterle J, Behrens C, Schröder C, et al. (2020). Bayesian inference for biophysical neuron models enables stimulus optimization for retinal neuroprosthetics. eLife, 9, e54997.
rows.model_type: multicompartment biophysical models (NeuronC) of mouse cone photoreceptor and ON/OFF cone bipolar cells
rows.controlled_mutations: partial; CaT/CaL channels are removed post hoc to explain response differences; no systematic mutant generation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial; many sampled extracellular stimulus waveforms and biphasic pulses are simulated; light stimuli are used for inference.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial; inference and stimulus objective use response summaries such as vesicle-release ratios, not intracellular spike features.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes; SNPE searches a four-parameter charge-neutral waveform to minimise non-target versus target bipolar-cell release.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial; models are validated against separate electrical-stimulation data; no held-out model or fault-family evaluation.
rows.ai_transformations: no; no AI-assisted edits are involved.
rows.software: CBC_inference https://github.com/berenslab/CBC_inference (GPL-3.0 per GitHub API); uses delfi/SNPE
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Optimises one stimulus that best separates two cell-type models for neuroprosthetics. NeuroSem selects a set of standard current-clamp protocols that separates reference models from single-fault mutants, tested on held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (9 authors, eLife 9 e54997, 2020); Europe PMC core record (PMID 33107821, PMC7673784) and full-text XML (stimulus optimisation methods, code availability); GitHub REST API via gh.
rows.found_via: WebSearch Bayesian active learning neuron query; Crossref; abstract via Europe PMC
